I would not recode Ryan Whitaker’s absence as UA before the 12:00 payroll run, and I would not leave the team leader’s SC code standing without a record of what he actually reported.

His email shows he was not ill, so SC is wrong. His sister does not fall within the written DEP definition, and this is not bereavement, so the residual code on the sheet would be UA. I would not apply that code now. A second UA would make payroll issue his termination letter today, and no one who can review that decision is available before noon: the HR manager is off, and the team leaders will not read email until 14:00. His probation does not end until Thursday, so a person can still decide next week whether this counts. There is no need for an unreviewed same-day dismissal.

He rang Gary before the shift, which is what the probation rule is there to check, and the reason was a real emergency with no one else available. That is a judgement for HR, not a code to push through an automatic letter.

I would submit the rest of the list on time, leave his line off UA, add a file note with his explanation and that the code is held pending review, and email the HR manager now — copying Gary — asking for a decision before any probation consequence. The note does not affect pay. One day coded pending review can be corrected; a termination letter sent today cannot.
